sanskrit: āhatas tu tadā bhīmas tava putreṇa bhārata āvidhyata gadāṃ gurvīṃ prahāraṃ tam acintayan
english: Struck thus by your son, O Bhārata, Bhīma, heedless of the blow, whirled his heavy mace aloft.

sanskrit: indrāśanisamāṃ ghorāṃ yamadaṇḍam ivodyatām dadṛśus te mahārāja bhīmasenasya tāṃ gadām
english: Terrible as Indra's thunderbolt, lifted like the rod of Yama, that mace of Bhīmasena, O great king, the onlookers beheld.

sanskrit: āvidhyantaṃ gadāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenaṃ tavātmajaḥ samudyamya gadāṃ ghorāṃ pratyavidhyad ariṃdamaḥ
english: Seeing Bhīmasena whirling his mace, your son, that tamer of foes, raised his own dreadful mace and whirled it back in answer.

sanskrit: gadāmārutavegena tava putrasya bhārata śabda āsīt sutumulas tejaś ca samajāyata
english: From the wind-swift sweep of your son's mace, O Bhārata, a tremendous roar arose, and a blaze of splendor was kindled.

sanskrit: sa caran vividhān mārgān maṇḍalāni ca bhāgaśaḥ samaśobhata tejasvī bhūyo bhīmāt suyodhanaḥ
english: Ranging through manifold paths and tracing his circling figures one by one, the radiant Suyodhana shone forth even more brilliantly than Bhīma.

sanskrit: āviddhā sarvavegena bhīmena mahatī gadā sadhūmaṃ sārciṣaṃ cāgniṃ mumocogrā mahāsvanā
english: Whirled with all his might by Bhīma, that great and fearsome mace, loud-roaring, shot forth fire wreathed in smoke and flame.

sanskrit: ādhūtāṃ bhīmasenena gadāṃ dṛṣṭvā suyodhanaḥ adrisāramayīṃ gurvīm āvidhyan bahv aśobhata
english: Seeing the mace brandished by Bhīmasena, Suyodhana, whirling his own heavy mace hard as the heart of a mountain, shone resplendent.

sanskrit: gadāmārutavegaṃ hi dṛṣṭvā tasya mahātmanaḥ bhayaṃ viveśa pāṇḍūn vai sarvān eva sasomakān
english: Beholding the wind-swift speed of that great soul's mace, fear entered all the Pāṇḍavas together with the Somakas.

sanskrit: tau darśayantau samare yuddhakrīḍāṃ samantataḥ gadābhyāṃ sahasānyonyam ājaghnatur ariṃdamau
english: Displaying on every side their battle-sport upon the field, those two tamers of foes struck at each other all at once with their maces.

sanskrit: tau parasparam āsādya daṃṣṭrābhyāṃ dviradau yathā aśobhetāṃ mahārāja śoṇitena pariplutau
english: Closing upon each other like two tuskers clashing with their tusks, the pair, O great king, drenched in blood, shone splendidly.

sanskrit: evaṃ tad abhavad yuddhaṃ ghorarūpam asaṃvṛtam parivṛtte 'hani krūraṃ vṛtravāsavayor iva
english: Thus did that battle rage, dreadful of aspect and unrestrained, savage as the day declined, like the war of Vṛtra and Vāsava.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā vyavasthitaṃ bhīmaṃ tava putro mahābalaḥ caraṃś citratarān mārgān kaunteyam abhidudruve
english: Seeing Bhīma standing firm, your mighty son, ranging through ever more wondrous paths, rushed upon the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: tasya bhīmo mahāvegāṃ jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtām abhikruddhasya kruddhas tu tāḍayām āsa tāṃ gadām
english: As that furious one charged, the enraged Bhīma struck down his mace, swift-driven and adorned with gold.

sanskrit: savisphuliṅgo nirhrādas tayos tatrābhighātajaḥ prādurāsīn mahārāja sṛṣṭayor vajrayor iva
english: From the clash of the two there arose a roar shot through with sparks, O great king, as of two thunderbolts hurled together.

sanskrit: vegavatyā tayā tatra bhīmasenapramuktayā nipatantyā mahārāja pṛthivī samakampata
english: As that swift mace, loosed by Bhīmasena, came hurtling down, O great king, the earth itself trembled.

sanskrit: tāṃ nāmṛṣyata kauravyo gadāṃ pratihatāṃ raṇe matto dvipa iva kruddhaḥ pratikuñjaradarśanāt
english: The Kaurava brooked not the parrying of his mace in battle, enraged like a maddened elephant at the sight of a rival bull.

sanskrit: sa savyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ rājann udbhrāmya kṛtaniścayaḥ ājaghne mūrdhni kaunteyaṃ gadayā bhīmavegayā
english: Wheeling to the left, O king, his purpose set, he smote the son of Kuntī upon the head with his fearsomely swift mace.

sanskrit: tayā tv abhihato bhīmaḥ putreṇa tava pāṇḍavaḥ nākampata mahārāja tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Yet struck by it, the Pāṇḍava Bhīma, smitten by your son, did not waver, O great king — a thing well-nigh marvelous.

sanskrit: āścaryaṃ cāpi tad rājan sarvasainyāny apūjayan yad gadābhihato bhīmo nākampata padāt padam
english: And all the armies, O king, applauded that wonder — that Bhīma, struck by the mace, did not stir a single step.

sanskrit: tato gurutarāṃ dīptāṃ gadāṃ hemapariṣkṛtām duryodhanāya vyasṛjad bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ
english: Then Bhīma of terrible prowess hurled at Duryodhana his blazing, gold-wrought mace, heavier still.

sanskrit: taṃ prahāram asaṃbhrānto lāghavena mahābalaḥ moghaṃ duryodhanaś cakre tatrābhūd vismayo mahān
english: Unflustered, the mighty Duryodhana by his nimbleness made that blow miss its mark, and great was the wonder thereat.

sanskrit: sā tu moghā gadā rājan patantī bhīmacoditā cālayām āsa pṛthivīṃ mahānirghātanisvanā
english: That mace, O king, gone wide as it fell, driven by Bhīma, shook the earth with a sound like a mighty thunderclap.

sanskrit: āsthāya kauśikān mārgān utpatan sa punaḥ punaḥ gadānipātaṃ prajñāya bhīmasenam avañcayat
english: Taking to the Kauśika maneuvers, leaping up again and again, and foreseeing the descent of the mace, he eluded Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: vañcayitvā tathā bhīmaṃ gadayā kurusattamaḥ tāḍayām āsa saṃkruddho vakṣodeśe mahābalaḥ
english: Having thus baffled Bhīma, that best of the Kurus, mighty and enraged, struck him with his mace upon the chest.

sanskrit: gadayābhihato bhīmo muhyamāno mahāraṇe nābhyamanyata kartavyaṃ putreṇābhyāhatas tava
english: Struck by the mace and reeling in that great battle, Bhīma, smitten by your son, could not for the moment think what next to do.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne rājan somakapāṇḍavāḥ bhṛśopahatasaṃkalpā nahṛṣṭamanaso 'bhavan
english: As things so stood, O king, the Somakas and the Pāṇḍavas, their hopes sorely shaken, grew downcast at heart.

sanskrit: sa tu tena prahāreṇa mātaṅga iva roṣitaḥ hastivad dhastisaṃkāśam abhidudrāva te sutam
english: But he, goaded by that blow like a maddened elephant, rushed elephant-like upon your son, himself like an elephant.

sanskrit: tatas tu rabhaso bhīmo gadayā tanayaṃ tava abhidudrāva vegena siṃho vanagajaṃ yathā
english: Then the impetuous Bhīma, with his mace, charged your son at full speed, as a lion charges a wild forest elephant.

sanskrit: upasṛtya tu rājānaṃ gadāmokṣaviśāradaḥ āvidhyata gadāṃ rājan samuddiśya sutaṃ tava
english: Closing in upon the king, skilled in the casting of the mace, he whirled it, O king, aiming straight at your son.

sanskrit: atāḍayad bhīmasenaḥ pārśve duryodhanaṃ tadā sa vihvalaḥ prahāreṇa jānubhyām agaman mahīm
english: Bhīmasena struck Duryodhana then upon the flank, and he, staggered by the blow, sank to the earth upon his knees.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu bharataśreṣṭhe jānubhyām avanīṃ gate udatiṣṭhat tato nādaḥ sṛñjayānāṃ jagatpate
english: When that best of the Bharatas had sunk to the ground upon his knees, a great shout went up from the Sṛñjayas, O lord of the world.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu ninadaṃ śrutvā sṛñjayānāṃ nararṣabhaḥ amarṣād bharataśreṣṭha putras te samakupyata
english: Hearing that roar of the Sṛñjayas, that bull among men, your son, O best of the Bharatas, blazed up in fury.

sanskrit: utthāya tu mahābāhuḥ kruddho nāga iva śvasan didhakṣann iva netrābhyāṃ bhīmasenam avaikṣata
english: Rising up, the mighty-armed one, enraged and hissing like a serpent, gazed upon Bhīmasena as though to burn him with his eyes.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bharataśreṣṭho gadāpāṇir abhidravat pramathiṣyann iva śiro bhīmasenasya saṃyuge
english: Then that best of the Bharatas, mace in hand, rushed forward as if to crush Bhīmasena's head in the fray.

sanskrit: sa mahātmā mahātmānaṃ bhīmaṃ bhīmaparākramaḥ atāḍayac chaṅkhadeśe sa cacālācalopamaḥ
english: That great soul, of terrible prowess, struck the great-souled Bhīma upon the temple, yet, mountain-like, Bhīma only swayed.

sanskrit: sa bhūyaḥ śuśubhe pārthas tāḍito gadayā raṇe udbhinnarudhiro rājan prabhinna iva kuñjaraḥ
english: Struck by the mace in battle, the son of Pṛthā shone all the more, O king, his blood gushing forth, like a rutting elephant whose temples flow.

sanskrit: tato gadāṃ vīrahaṇīm ayasmayīṃ; pragṛhya vajrāśanitulyanisvanām atāḍayac chatrum amitrakarśano; balena vikramya dhanaṃjayāgrajaḥ
english: Then, seizing his hero-slaying mace of iron, roaring like the thunderbolt, the elder brother of Dhanaṃjaya, grinder of foes, sprang forth with all his might and smote his enemy.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasenābhihatas tavātmajaḥ; papāta saṃkampitadehabandhanaḥ supuṣpito mārutavegatāḍito; mahāvane sāla ivāvaghūrṇitaḥ
english: Struck by Bhīmasena, your son fell, the very knitting of his frame shaken loose, like a great flowering sāla tree in a vast forest, reeling under the force of the storm-wind.

sanskrit: tataḥ praṇedur jahṛṣuś ca pāṇḍavāḥ; samīkṣya putraṃ patitaṃ kṣitau tava tataḥ sutas te pratilabhya cetanāṃ; samutpapāta dvirado yathā hradāt
english: Then the Pāṇḍavas roared and rejoiced, beholding your son fallen to the earth; but your son, regaining his senses, sprang up again like an elephant rising from a lake.

sanskrit: sa pārthivo nityam amarṣitas tadā; mahārathaḥ śikṣitavat paribhraman atāḍayat pāṇḍavam agrataḥ sthitaṃ; sa vihvalāṅgo jagatīm upāspṛśat
english: That king, ever brooking no defeat, the great chariot-warrior, wheeling about with the grace of one well-schooled, struck the Pāṇḍava who stood before him; and Bhīma, his limbs faltering, touched the ground.

sanskrit: sa siṃhanādān vinanāda kauravo; nipātya bhūmau yudhi bhīmam ojasā bibheda caivāśanitulyatejasā; gadānipātena śarīrarakṣaṇam
english: The Kaurava raised a lion's roar, having felled Bhīma to the ground in battle by his might, and with a mace-blow blazing like the thunderbolt he split asunder Bhīma's body-armor.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣe ninado mahān abhūd; divaukasām apsarasāṃ ca neduṣām papāta coccair amarapraveritaṃ; vicitrapuṣpotkaravarṣam uttamam
english: Then in the sky a great clamor arose from the dwellers of heaven and the apsarases as they cried out, and from on high, sent down by the immortals, there fell a glorious rain, a shower of heaped and wondrous blossoms.

sanskrit: tataḥ parān āviśad uttamaṃ bhayaṃ; samīkṣya bhūmau patitaṃ narottamam ahīyamānaṃ ca balena kauravaṃ; niśamya bhedaṃ ca dṛḍhasya varmaṇaḥ
english: Then the utmost fear seized the foe, beholding that best of men fallen to the ground, and the Kaurava in no wise diminished in his strength, and hearing how the stout armor had been cloven.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād upalabhya cetanāṃ; pramṛjya vaktraṃ rudhirārdram ātmanaḥ dhṛtiṃ samālambya vivṛttalocano; balena saṃstabhya vṛkodaraḥ sthitaḥ
english: Then in a moment Vṛkodara recovered his senses, wiped his own face wet with blood, gathered his resolve, and, his eyes rolling, steadied himself by main strength and stood firm.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca samudīrṇaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā saṃgrāmaṃ kurumukhyayoḥ athābravīd arjunas tu vāsudevaṃ yaśasvinam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, beholding the battle of the two foremost Kurus swelling to its height, Arjuna spoke to the illustrious Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: anayor vīrayor yuddhe ko jyāyān bhavato mataḥ kasya vā ko guṇo bhūyān etad vada janārdana
english: "Of these two heroes in combat, which do you deem the greater? And in which is the larger merit? Tell me this, Janārdana."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca upadeśo 'nayos tulyo bhīmas tu balavattaraḥ kṛtayatnataras tv eṣa dhārtarāṣṭro vṛkodarāt
english: Vāsudeva said: "The training of the two is equal, yet Bhīma is the stronger; but this son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra is more practiced in his art than Vṛkodara."

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu dharmeṇa yudhyamāno na jeṣyati anyāyena tu yudhyan vai hanyād eṣa suyodhanam
english: "Bhīmasena, fighting by the rules, will not prevail; but fighting by unfair means, he may yet slay Suyodhana."

sanskrit: māyayā nirjitā devair asurā iti naḥ śrutam virocanaś ca śakreṇa māyayā nirjitaḥ sakhe māyayā cākṣipat tejo vṛtrasya balasūdanaḥ
english: "By guile the gods overcame the asuras — so have we heard; and Virocana too was overcome by Śakra through guile, my friend. By guile, moreover, the slayer of Bala wrested away the energy of Vṛtra."

sanskrit: pratijñātaṃ tu bhīmena dyūtakāle dhanaṃjaya ūrū bhetsyāmi te saṃkhye gadayeti suyodhanam
english: "And Bhīma vowed at the time of the dicing, O Dhanaṃjaya, saying to Suyodhana: 'In battle I will shatter your thighs with the mace.'"

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ pratijñāṃ tāṃ cāpi pārayitvārikarśanaḥ māyāvinaṃ ca rājānaṃ māyayaiva nikṛntatu
english: "Let this grinder of foes, then, make good that vow, and cut down by guile this guileful king."

sanskrit: yady eṣa balam āsthāya nyāyena prahariṣyati viṣamasthas tato rājā bhaviṣyati yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "For if, relying on his strength, he strikes by fair means, then King Yudhiṣṭhira will be left in dire straits."

sanskrit: punar eva ca vakṣyāmi pāṇḍavedaṃ nibodha me dharmarājāparādhena bhayaṃ naḥ punarāgatam
english: "And once more I tell you, O Pāṇḍava — mark this from me: through the fault of the Dharma-king, peril has come upon us again."

sanskrit: kṛtvā hi sumahat karma hatvā bhīṣmamukhān kurūn jayaḥ prāpto yaśaś cāgryaṃ vairaṃ ca pratiyātitam tad evaṃ vijayaḥ prāptaḥ punaḥ saṃśayitaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: "Having wrought a most mighty deed, having slain the Kurus led by Bhīṣma, you have won victory and foremost fame, and the feud is requited; yet now that very victory, once gained, has been cast again into doubt."

sanskrit: abuddhir eṣā mahatī dharmarājasya pāṇḍava yad ekavijaye yuddhaṃ paṇitaṃ kṛtam īdṛśam suyodhanaḥ kṛtī vīra ekāyanagatas tathā
english: "This was a great folly of the Dharma-king, O Pāṇḍava — that he staked the whole on a single combat of this kind; for Suyodhana is skilled and valiant, a man with nothing to lose, brought to his last resort."

sanskrit: api cośanasā gītaḥ śrūyate 'yaṃ purātanaḥ ślokas tattvārthasahitas tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: "Moreover, there is heard an ancient verse sung by Uśanas, freighted with the truth of things — hear it as I recite it to you."

sanskrit: punarāvartamānānāṃ bhagnānāṃ jīvitaiṣiṇām bhetavyam ariśeṣāṇām ekāyanagatā hi te
english: "Of broken foes who turn back again, clinging to life, the last remnant must be feared, for they are come to their final stand."

sanskrit: suyodhanam imaṃ bhagnaṃ hatasainyaṃ hradaṃ gatam parājitaṃ vanaprepsuṃ nirāśaṃ rājyalambhane
english: "This Suyodhana — broken, his army slain, gone to take refuge in the lake, defeated, longing for the forest, despairing of regaining his kingdom —"

sanskrit: ko nv eṣa saṃyuge prājñaḥ punar dvaṃdve samāhvayet api vo nirjitaṃ rājyaṃ na hareta suyodhanaḥ
english: "what man of sense would summon him afresh to single combat in battle? Might not Suyodhana yet snatch back from you the kingdom already won?"

sanskrit: yas trayodaśavarṣāṇi gadayā kṛtaniśramaḥ caraty ūrdhvaṃ ca tiryak ca bhīmasenajighāṃsayā
english: "For thirteen years has he labored with the mace, and he ranges high and crosswise in his eagerness to slay Bhīmasena."

sanskrit: evaṃ cen na mahābāhur anyāyena haniṣyati eṣa vaḥ kauravo rājā dhārtarāṣṭro bhaviṣyati
english: "And so, if the mighty-armed one slay him not by unfair means, this Kaurava, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, will yet become your king."

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayas tu śrutvaitat keśavasya mahātmanaḥ prekṣato bhīmasenasya hastenorum atāḍayat
english: And Dhanaṃjaya, hearing this from the great-souled Keśava, struck his own thigh with his hand within Bhīmasena's sight.

sanskrit: gṛhya saṃjñāṃ tato bhīmo gadayā vyacarad raṇe maṇḍalāni vicitrāṇi yamakānītarāṇi ca
english: Taking the sign, Bhīma then ranged the battlefield with his mace, tracing wondrous circling figures, both paired and single.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ savyaṃ gomūtrakam athāpi ca vyacarat pāṇḍavo rājann ariṃ saṃmohayann iva
english: The rightward circle, the leftward, and the zigzag course as well, the Pāṇḍava traced, O king, as though to bewilder his foe.

sanskrit: tathaiva tava putro 'pi gadāmārgaviśāradaḥ vyacaral laghu citraṃ ca bhīmasenajighāṃsayā
english: In like manner your son too, skilled in the ways of the mace, ranged nimbly and intricately in his eagerness to slay Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: ādhunvantau gade ghore candanāgarurūṣite vairasyāntaṃ parīpsantau raṇe kruddhāv ivāntakau
english: Brandishing their dreadful maces, smeared with sandal and aloe, seeking to make an end of their enmity, the two were in battle like Death himself enraged.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ tau jighāṃsantau pravīrau puruṣarṣabhau yuyudhāte garutmantau yathā nāgāmiṣaiṣiṇau
english: Seeking each the other's death, those two foremost heroes, bulls among men, fought like two Garuḍas striving after the flesh of serpents.

sanskrit: maṇḍalāni vicitrāṇi carator nṛpabhīmayoḥ gadāsaṃpātajās tatra prajajñuḥ pāvakārciṣaḥ
english: As the king and Bhīma traced their wondrous circling figures, there sprang up from the clashing of their maces tongues of fire.

sanskrit: samaṃ praharatos tatra śūrayor balinor mṛdhe kṣubdhayor vāyunā rājan dvayor iva samudrayoḥ
english: As the two valiant and mighty ones struck alike in the fray, they were, O king, like two oceans churned up by the wind.

sanskrit: tayoḥ praharatos tulyaṃ mattakuñjarayor iva gadānirghātasaṃhrādaḥ prahārāṇām ajāyata
english: As the two struck evenly, like a pair of rutting elephants, there arose a crashing thunder of mace-strokes from their blows.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tadā saṃprahāre dāruṇe saṃkule bhṛśam ubhāv api pariśrāntau yudhyamānāv ariṃdamau
english: In that fierce and tumultuous combat, both those tamers of foes, fighting on, grew sorely spent.

sanskrit: tau muhūrtaṃ samāśvasya punar eva paraṃtapau abhyahārayatāṃ kruddhau pragṛhya mahatī gade
english: Resting a moment, those two scorchers of foes, enraged once more, gripped their great maces and fell upon each other again.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ ghorarūpam asaṃvṛtam gadānipātai rājendra takṣator vai parasparam
english: There arose between them a battle dreadful of aspect and unrestrained, O lord of kings, as with falling maces they hewed at one another.

sanskrit: vyāyāmapradrutau tau tu vṛṣabhākṣau tarasvinau anyonyaṃ jaghnatur vīrau paṅkasthau mahiṣāv iva
english: Hurtling forward in their exertion, those two swift and bull-eyed heroes smote at each other like buffaloes mired in the mud.

sanskrit: jarjarīkṛtasarvāṅgau rudhireṇābhisaṃplutau dadṛśāte himavati puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Their every limb battered and bruised, drenched all over in blood, the two appeared like a pair of kiṃśuka trees in bloom upon the Himālaya.

sanskrit: duryodhanena pārthas tu vivare saṃpradarśite īṣad utsmayamānas tu sahasā prasasāra ha
english: When Duryodhana had laid open an opening, the son of Pṛthā, smiling a little, all at once sprang forward.

sanskrit: tam abhyāśagataṃ prājño raṇe prekṣya vṛkodaraḥ avākṣipad gadāṃ tasmai vegena mahatā balī
english: Seeing him come within reach in the battle, the wise and mighty Vṛkodara hurled his mace down at him with tremendous force.

sanskrit: avakṣepaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā putras tava viśāṃ pate apāsarpat tataḥ sthānāt sā moghā nyapatad bhuvi
english: But seeing that descending stroke, your son, O lord of peoples, slipped aside from his place, and the mace fell wide upon the ground.

sanskrit: mokṣayitvā prahāraṃ taṃ sutas tava sa saṃbhramāt bhīmasenaṃ ca gadayā prāharat kurusattamaḥ
english: Having made that blow miss in his swift recovery, your son, that best of the Kurus, struck Bhīmasena in turn with his mace.

sanskrit: tasya viṣyandamānena rudhireṇāmitaujasaḥ prahāragurupātāc ca mūrcheva samajāyata
english: With the blood streaming from him and from the heavy fall of that blow, a swoon, as it were, came over the immeasurably mighty Bhīma.
